claim: LangGraph is an agent orchestration framework emphasizing durable execution, streaming, human-in-the-loop, persistence, and long-running agents.
notes: Official LangGraph docs state durable execution, streaming, human-in-the-loop and agent orchestration capabilities.

claim: LangGraph supports human-in-the-loop interrupts that pause graph execution, persist state, and resume after external input.
notes: Official interrupt docs describe pause/resume behavior and JSON-serializable interrupt payloads.

claim: Haystack is an open-source framework for production-ready AI agents, RAG applications, and scalable multimodal search systems.
notes: Official Haystack intro uses this positioning and describes reusable pipeline components.

claim: RAGFlow is an open-source RAG engine based on deep document understanding and supports citations over complex formatted data.
notes: Official quickstart describes deep document understanding, datasets, parsing intervention, and cited AI chat.

claim: RAGFlow GitHub positions the project as a RAG engine fusing RAG with agent capabilities and deep document understanding-based extraction.
notes: GitHub README confirms deep document understanding extraction and Agent capability framing.

claim: Open WebUI includes Knowledge & RAG features for uploaded files, knowledge bases, vector search, full-content injection, and retrieval over knowledge bases.
notes: Official features page describes Knowledge & RAG and native function-calling-based retrieval.

claim: Open WebUI supports changing the RAG embedding model in Admin Panel settings and supports Ollama/OpenAI embedding models.
notes: Official RAG docs state embedding model support and Admin Panel path.

claim: ComfyUI official docs cover custom nodes, local API integration, built-in nodes, cloud API, and MCP-related cloud integration.
notes: Official docs homepage lists Custom Nodes, Local API, Built-in Nodes, Cloud API, and Cloud MCP Server.

claim: ComfyUI custom node installation commonly involves cloning repos into the ComfyUI custom_nodes directory; official docs use ComfyUI-Manager as an example repository.
notes: Official custom node docs describe navigating to custom_nodes and git cloning node code.

claim: ComfyUI-Manager fetches local update data and applies updates through the Install Custom Nodes menu update button.
notes: Official README excerpt confirms Fetch Updates vs Update button behavior.

claim: Gradio ChatInterface is the high-level abstraction for building web chatbot UIs around a function using user input and chat history.
notes: Official ChatInterface docs state it is a high-level abstraction for chatbot UIs.

claim: Gradio session state persists across multiple submits in a page session, is not shared between users, and does not persist after refresh.
notes: Official state guide provides exactly this session-state behavior.

claim: Gradio Interface is the main high-level class for creating a web GUI/demo around a Python function or machine learning model.
notes: Official Interface docs state it wraps a function with input/output components.

claim: Document chunking is a consequential RAG design decision because it determines the units stored, retrieved, and processed by AI systems.
notes: LlamaIndex glossary states chunking breaks large documents into smaller segments for storage, retrieval, and processing, and affects answer quality.

claim: Chunk size should be empirically evaluated for a given RAG system rather than fixed blindly.
notes: LlamaIndex blog explicitly frames ideal chunk size as something to evaluate with response evaluation.
